RC-03: R32: rule "Capture it at rest, then press and hold the mouse button on it without releasing and capture it again. Yes when the held button looks visibly different from its resting look". Holding the button means the pointer is on it, so the held capture always shows the pointed-at tone lift that R38 already grades. Any app that passes R38 passes R32 whether or not it has a pressed state: a judge who answers R38 already knows R32, and R32 grades nothing of its own (C-UX-50). -> Replace the text. criterion: "Holding the mouse button down on Go to Gallery shows a pressed look distinct from its pointed-at look." evaluation_rule: "Go to Gallery is the filled button at the foot of the AURA introduction. Rest the mouse on it without pressing, wait for its tone change to finish and capture it. Then press and hold the mouse button without moving or releasing, and capture it again. Yes when the held button looks visibly different from the pointed-at capture, such as a further change of tone, a slight inset or a scale change. No when the held button looks the same as the pointed-at capture."

The verdict depends on a different control on a different page: if Go to Gallery's glide is broken, R33 has nothing to compare against. "Within the first few captures" is undefined.
